content:
Morgan: thinking about a lightweight compatibility layer for precision profiles — idea is an aliasing table that maps older profile names and bitwidths to runtime-compatible fallbacks. Keeps customers from needing profile rewrites.
Liam: +1, can we make it programmable per-tenant? some enterprise customers want to lock to int8 only.
Sasha: per-tenant overrides make sense, but we need clear semantics: aliasing for name -> runtime mapping vs active re-quant at load time. Different costs.
Claire: two modes: 1) name alias (no compute change, runtime chooses compatible kernel) 2) convert-on-deploy (one-time re-quant/convert artifacts so runtime treats like native).
Anita: convert-on-deploy is heavier disk/CI but avoids on-the-fly perf regressions. name-alias is quick but may cause subtle quality shifts if we silently swap fp8->int8 kernels.
Morgan: propose default = name-alias for dev/staging, convert-on-deploy for dedicated/private by customer opt-in. Add opt-out flag for hosted customers who want strict fidelity.
Liam: telemetry question — how do we track if aliasing caused quality regression? need per-profile degradation score tags and a hook in eval pipeline.
Sasha: add a header in request trace: X-precision-alias: {original, resolved}. Runtime should log resolved profile + kernel used. Then our eval can join traces with sample prompts to compute deg_score.
Claire: ops-bot: deploy hint: config example ->
```
precision_aliasing:
  default: alias
  tenants:
    acme-corp: convert
  mapping:
    "redwood/fp8/small": "redwood/int8/small-v2"
```
Anita: also surface an API to list effective profile for a model id. UI/console should show when aliasing is active and link to quality report.
Morgan: perf thought — if aliasing maps to int8 kernel, we might need a short warmup to populate kv cache; make sure canary smoke includes a few warmup requests to avoid cold-latency spikes.
Liam: migration: add a lint step in model onboarding to detect ambiguous profiles (same name but different semantics). warn owners if aliasing will be applied.
Sasha: ops question: rollback story? if aliasing causes issues we should flip to convert-on-deploy or force original bits. We need an ops playbook entry.
Claire: +1, add a runbook: detect spike in deg_score > threshold -> pause aliasing for that model id, notify owner, auto-trigger shadow replay comparing outputs.
Anita: one more: ensure model-signature includes quantization fingerprint (scale/zero points or affine params) so we can better decide safe aliases. Not just bitwidth.
Morgan: action items: 1) design alias table schema (Liam) 2) runtime logging patch for X-precision-alias header (Sasha) 3) console UI indicator and list API (Anita/Claire) 4) eval integration for deg_score joins (Liam/Sasha).
ops-bot: note created: runbook-ticket#8421 created, assigned to eng-ml.
Liam: I'll start the alias table proto this afternoon, ping me if you have edge cases.
Sasha: I'll prototype the header + kernel-tag logging. expect a PoC next week.
Morgan: cool — let's keep aliasing opt-in per model until we have solid telemetry. :thumbsup:
Claire: also flag for privacy: ensure telemetry sampling obeys tenant data retention settings.
Anita: ack, adding to spec.
Morgan: thanks all, we'll sync on Thursday for design review.
